However, building finely detailed mountain scenery can be a daunting task when using time consuming traditional methods, such as carving wet plaster or by stacking multiple small plaster castings to build larger rock walls. For a better solution, consider using rubber rock castings from Cripplebush Valley Models. This firm offers lightweight, highly detailed, ready to install rubber rock castings. They come pre-colored in sturdy, yet still flexible rubber material, allowing you to produce mountain scenery quickly and easily on your toy train layout. candidates.title: Repurposed railroad equipment
candidates.excerpt: Q: I recently saw an announcement for Athearn’s new HO scale concession cupola caboose sets. Three of the cabooses were converted to serve food (ice cream, hot dogs, and pizza) and one is decorated in a patriotic motif for the chamber of commerce. What are some other examples of repurposed railroad equipment? — Buddy C. A: Though we think of recycling as a relatively modern concept, railroads have been reusing equipment for years. Boxcars, cabooses, and passenger equipment have been converted to yard offices and maintenance-of-way storage sheds by numerous railroads. One of my favorite examples of railroad recycling is the sand tower at Wisconsin Central’s (now Canadian National’s) North Fond du Lac, Wis., yard. It was fashioned, in part, out of a modified two-bay offset-side hopper. Kazuo Terasawa shared how he modeled it in HO scale in the June 2011 issue of Model Railroader. candidates.title: Maersk lowers Australia and New Zealand intermodal fuel fees
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will reduce its Intermodal Fuel Fees for landside transportation services in Australia and New Zealand from 1 December 2026. Across five Australian states, the fee will fall from 25% to 22%. In New Zealand, it will decrease from 27% to 23%. The announced levels will apply from 1 December 2026 through 31 January 2027, although Maersk said it will continue reviewing the charges monthly. Australia Intermodal Fuel Fee New Zealand Intermodal Fuel Fee Maersk introduced the Intermodal Fuel Fee on 16 March 2026. The charge appears as EFS for export movements and IFS for imports. The carrier attributed the measure to global energy costs and fuel availability pressures associated with the security situation in the Middle East. Maersk said further revisions may be introduced as market conditions develop.

candidates.title: Maersk introduces document amendment fee in North America
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will introduce a Transport Document Amendment Fee for certain shipments loading from ports in the United States and Canada. The charge will take effect on 1 January 2027. A fee of US$75 will apply to eligible amendment requests submitted three or more calendar days after the containers have been loaded aboard the vessel at the first load port. Maersk refers to the new timeframe as the “Laden on Board + 3 Day Rule”. The fee will cover late changes to transport document details, including requests to change the document type from a negotiable Bill of Lading to a Sea Waybill or vice versa. Amendments excluded from the fee The charge will not apply to: - Seal number additions or modifications - Mandatory reference changes required for regulatory or compliance purposes - House Bill of Lading requests, amendments or cancellations - Out-of-gauge shipments Maersk noted that the fee may still apply when a single request combines an excluded amendment with other chargeable document change

candidates.title: Maersk storms into megamax league
candidates.excerpt: Danish liner giant AP Moller-Maersk has confirmed an order for 12 ultra-large containerships of 24,000 teu, marking its entry into the largest boxship segment with an investment estimated at around $2.9bn. The Copenhagen-based group said the dual-fuel vessels would be delivered in 2030 and 2031, becoming the biggest ships in its fleet. Each vessel will be equipped with engines capable of running on conventional marine fuel or LNG, with the 12-ship series adding 288,000 teu of nominal capacity. Maersk has declined to identify the shipbuilder or disclose the contract value. Shipbuilding sources have previously put the price of the vessels at around $240m apiece. The order follows weeks of negotiations with Chinese shipbuilders, with both Hengli Heavy Industries and Hudong-Zhonghua linked to the project. candidates.excerpt: Greek containership owner Danaos has secured another $611m in contracted revenue through a string of new fixtures and charter extensions, taking its forward revenue backlog to $5bn. The John Coustas-led company revealed the deals in its latest quarterly update, with a comparison of its fleet employment schedules showing fresh contracts for six containership newbuildings alongside longer employment for several ships already on the water. Four 5,300 teu vessels ordered at CSSC’s Huangpu Wenchong Shipyard earlier this year have secured three-year charters. The quartet, scheduled for delivery in 2028 and 2029, was previously listed without employment. Another two 9,000 teu newbuildings booked in September for delivery in early 2029 have secured charters running for at least 4.8 years. US rail traffic rises 7.3% as intermodal gains 10.7% in latest week
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
